page: Microsoft Azure L16as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine based on the Lasv4 instance family. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Compute resources include 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache configuration consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (with F, VNNI, and BF16 extensions), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 128.0 GB of RAM, allocating 8.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled as a 3,840 GB NVMe SSD, providing dense high-speed local disk capacity. The configuration does not include a hardware accelerator or GPU, nor does it supply complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3,078.29 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2,084.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core compute metrics settle in the average range, including a multi-core stress-ng result of 24,638.26 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 12,317.0. Memory tests indicate average small-block cached read bandwidth at 1,216.02 GB/sec and average large-block write bandwidth at 27.94 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read bandwidth scored in the lower 25% at 37.93 GB/sec.

In operational benchmarks, the instance produced 22.44 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 20.17 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For CPU-based machine learning inference, small model (135M) generation reached the top 25% at 274.17 tokens per second, but larger 70B model prompt processing settled in the bottom 10% at 4.44 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

Given its 3,840 GB NVMe SSD and 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, Microsoft Azure L16as_v4 is well suited for high-throughput relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, data warehousing, and log analytics pipelines requiring dense local disk performance alongside consistent single-threaded execution.
description: Microsoft Azure L16as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 128.0 GB of system memory, and a 3,840 GB NVMe SSD. It does not include dedicated GPU accelerators. Synthetic evaluations demonstrate strong single-core performance, supported by top-tier stress-ng and Geekbench single-core results, alongside steady middle-tier multi-core and memory write metrics. While large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is comparatively limited and large-parameter language model processing is constrained, transactional capacity remains solid with 22.44 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance provides an efficient profile for I/O-intensive workloads including transactional databases, high-capacity NoSQL clusters, search indexing, and real-time log ingestion requiring fast direct NVMe storage.
